target.title: fix(mac): opening General Settings crashes in packaged app
target.body:
Closes #111270

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening General Settings in the packaged macOS 2026.7.2 app would immediately crash when the Quick Chat shortcut recorder rendered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hand-built macOS app did not include KeyboardShortcuts' generated SwiftPM resource bundle. Swift 6.2's generated `Bundle.module` accessor already searches `Bundle.main.resourceURL`, so the package step now copies the generated bundle into the app's `Contents/Resources` directory and fails closed if it is missing. The packager also preserves the committed Swift package resolution byte-for-byte across resolve and build commands.

Regression coverage exercises both the package-script boundary and hosted General Settings construction, so a successful Swift compile alone cannot mask a broken distributable app.

## User Impact

Users can open General Settings and use the Quick Chat shortcut recorder without the macOS app terminating.

Release note: Fix macOS General Settings crashing when the Quick Chat shortcut recorder loads from a packaged app.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the 2026.7.2 failure as a main-thread `NSBundle.module` assertion from `KeyboardShortcuts.RecorderCocoa.configureView`; the installed bundle inventory lacked `KeyboardShortcuts_KeyboardShortcuts.bundle`.
- Focused package tests: 26 passed, 2 platform skips (28 total).
- Blacksmith changed gate passed, including formatting, dependency and package-patch guards, root test typechecking, script lint, and the macOS packaging lane (57 passed, 13 platform skips in the surrounding tooling and daemon shards).
- Built exact head `8cccc6fbbcf67215b7ae4bec2ec702c34b4b4611` as a packaged macOS app, signed it with Developer ID team `Y5PE65HELJ`, and passed `codesign --verify --deep --strict`. The app embedded the exact commit, contained the KeyboardShortcuts localization bundle, and preserved `Package.resolved` byte-for-byte.
- Native accessibility proof opened `OpenClaw Settings` from that exact app and rendered `General`, `Quick Chat`, and the configured `⌥Space` recorder. The exact packaged process remained alive through a second inspection after 15 seconds.
- Fresh autoreview found no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests, and validation; the maintainer reviewed the code and understands the change.
